Hip Flexor Stretch.cue: Kneel in a lunge, gently tuck your pelvis, and shift forward without arching your back.
Hip Flexor Stretch.easier: Pad the back knee, use a chair for balance, and keep the forward shift small.
Hip Flexor Stretch.harder: If comfortable, bend the back knee and gently hold the back foot without forcing the knee or arching.

Elephant Walks.cue: Fold forward with soft knees and slowly alternate straightening each leg without locking the knee.
Elephant Walks.easier: Rest your hands on a stable chair and keep both knees slightly bent.
Elephant Walks.harder: Lower your hands toward the floor while continuing slow, comfortable alternating knee extensions.

Pancake Stretch.cue: Sit with legs comfortably wide and hinge forward from your hips while breathing steadily.
Pancake Stretch.easier: Sit upright with your back against a wall and use a narrower leg position.
Pancake Stretch.harder: Reach farther forward from your hips while keeping the position comfortable and unforced.

Figure-Four Stretch.cue: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the other thigh, and gently draw that thigh toward you.
Figure-Four Stretch.easier: Leave the supporting foot on the floor and hold the ankle-over-thigh position without pulling.
Figure-Four Stretch.harder: Draw the supporting thigh slightly closer while keeping your pelvis comfortable and avoiding knee pressure.

Lat Stretch.cue: From hands and knees, reach forward with thumbs up and gently lower your chest without arching.
Lat Stretch.easier: Keep your hands closer and lower your chest only a little.
Lat Stretch.harder: If your shoulders allow, clasp your hands overhead and gently lower your chest farther.

Seated Side Bend.cue: Sit tall, reach one arm overhead, and bend sideways while keeping both sit bones down.
Seated Side Bend.easier: Sit on a firm chair and make a small overhead reach with your other hand supporting you.
Seated Side Bend.harder: Lengthen the overhead reach and bend a little farther without lifting either hip or twisting.

Standing Active Twist.cue: Stand tall, actively turn your torso to one side, and briefly hold without pulling with your hands.
Standing Active Twist.easier: Use a smaller turn and keep your arms relaxed beside you.
Standing Active Twist.harder: Turn a little farther under your own control without forcing your spine or knees.

Marching in Place.cue: Keep marching in place and swing your arms gently, starting slowly and building a comfortable rhythm.
Marching in Place.easier: Hold a stable chair and take small, low steps.
Marching in Place.harder: Raise your knees a little higher and increase your pace while remaining comfortable.

Heel Digs.cue: Alternate placing each heel forward with toes up, keeping a soft bend in the supporting knee.
Heel Digs.easier: Hold a stable chair and place each heel only a short distance forward.
Heel Digs.harder: Reach each heel slightly farther forward and add gentle opposite-arm punches.

Knee Lifts.cue: Keep alternating knee lifts toward the opposite hand while standing tall and keeping your back steady.
Knee Lifts.easier: Hold a stable chair and lift each knee only a little.
Knee Lifts.harder: Lift each knee slightly higher without leaning backward or speeding beyond control.

Shoulder Rolls.cue: March gently and roll both shoulders five times forward, then five times backward, repeating smoothly.
Shoulder Rolls.easier: Stand still or sit tall and make smaller shoulder circles.
Shoulder Rolls.harder: Make slightly larger comfortable circles while maintaining a gentle marching rhythm.

Knee Bends.cue: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and repeat shallow knee bends, lowering slowly and rising smoothly.
Knee Bends.easier: Hold a stable chair and use a very small bend.
Knee Bends.harder: Use a slightly deeper comfortable bend while keeping your heels down and movement controlled.

Supine Hamstring Stretch.cue: Lie on your back, hold behind one thigh, and gently straighten that knee until you feel a mild stretch.
Supine Hamstring Stretch.easier: Keep the lifted knee more bent and use a towel around the thigh if reaching is difficult.
Supine Hamstring Stretch.harder: Straighten the lifted leg a little more without locking the knee or pulling on the knee joint.

Knee-to-Chest Stretch.cue: Lie with knees bent, hug behind one knee, and gently bring it toward your chest with your back relaxed.
Knee-to-Chest Stretch.easier: Draw the knee only a little toward you and leave the other foot on the floor.
Knee-to-Chest Stretch.harder: Bring the knee a little closer while keeping your pelvis relaxed and avoiding pressure on the knee joint.

Cat-Cow.cue: On hands and knees, slowly alternate rounding your back and gently opening your chest as you breathe.
Cat-Cow.easier: Use a smaller spinal movement and pad your knees as needed.
Cat-Cow.harder: Explore a slightly larger comfortable range while staying slow and avoiding a forced back arch.

Knee Rolls.cue: Lie with knees bent and feet down, then slowly roll your knees side to side with shoulders supported.
Knee Rolls.easier: Move your knees only a short distance from the center.
Knee Rolls.harder: Let your knees travel a little farther while keeping the movement comfortable and unforced.

Doorway Chest Stretch.cue: Place both forearms on a doorway and step forward gently, staying upright with shoulders relaxed.
Doorway Chest Stretch.easier: Lower your elbows and take a smaller step forward.
Doorway Chest Stretch.harder: Take a slightly larger step without leaning, arching your back, or forcing your shoulders.

Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch.cue: Bring one arm across your chest and gently support it above the elbow while keeping the shoulder down.
Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch.easier: Keep the arm lower and draw it only slightly across your chest.
Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch.harder: Draw the upper arm a little closer without pressing on the elbow joint or shrugging.

Overhead Triceps Stretch.cue: Reach one hand behind your neck and support the raised elbow gently with your other hand.
Overhead Triceps Stretch.easier: Let your raised elbow stay wider and avoid pulling it inward.
Overhead Triceps Stretch.harder: Gently guide the elbow a little inward while keeping your ribs down and shoulder comfortable.

Neck Side Bend.cue: Sit tall and gently tilt one ear toward its shoulder, keeping the opposite shoulder down.
Neck Side Bend.easier: Use a tiny tilt and leave both arms relaxed.
Neck Side Bend.harder: Increase the tilt only slightly while keeping both shoulders down and never pulling on your head.
